title: Colombia's first domestic-servitude trafficking conviction (Vaupés to Bogotá)
summary: In September 2018 a Colombian court handed down the country's first conviction for trafficking in persons for domestic servitude, sentencing a Colombian woman (not named by UNODC) to 13 years and 2 months. The victim, an 18-year-old Indigenous woman from Vaupés, was promised domestic work and a salary of US$77. On arrival in Bogotá she was told she would get no pay for two months to cover her travel tickets, then another 20 months unpaid for a decorative item she had broken. She worked over 12 hours a day with restrictions on her freedom. The prosecution argued abuse of a position of vulnerability, citing a UNODC issue paper.
